criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies compound interrogatories violating FRCP 33(a)(1)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly discusses FRCP 33 numerical limits and states that compound subparts in Nos. 1–25 should be assessed, specifically identifying Nos. 2, 5, 9, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20, 21, and 24 as likely compound. This identifies more than the required six interrogatories as containing multiple discrete subparts.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Cites FRCP 33(a)(1) 25-interrogatory limit
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo discusses a 25-interrogatory limit including discrete subparts, but attributes it to the CMO and does not cite FRCP/Rule/Fed. R. Civ. P. 33(a)(1).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Concludes total discrete subparts exceed 25
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo notes that the interrogatories exceed the 25 limit because Plaintiff numbered 30 and suggests assessing compound subparts, but it does not actually perform a discrete-subpart count or identify a total count of at least 35.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Flags that Trident exceeded limit without leave of court
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly states that the CMO permits no more than 25 interrogatories including discrete subparts, that Plaintiff numbered 30, and recommends objecting to Nos. 26–30 as exceeding the limit while seeking withdrawal, stipulation, or leave.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Flags Interrogatory No. 7 as seeking privileged info
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo's section for Interrogatory No. 7 expressly flags privilege concerns, objecting to legal advice, attorney-client communications, and counsel-directed work product, and limits 'advice received' to nonprivileged operational advice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Flags Interrogatory No. 14 as seeking privileged info
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo's section for Interrogatory No. 14 expressly states to object to legal advice, attorney-client communications, and litigation work product concerning the renewal, and not to reveal counsel's advice or protected consultations. This flags No. 14 as implicating attorney-client privileged communications.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Flags Interrogatory No. 22 as seeking privileged info
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo’s section for Interrogatory No. 22 expressly objects to attorney-client advice, counsel-directed work product, litigation communications, and requests for legal advice, and instructs separation of ordinary-course review from attorney-directed investigation. Thus it flags No. 22 as implicating privileged information.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Recommends asserting attorney-client privilege
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly recommends asserting attorney-client privilege for multiple relevant interrogatories, including No. 7 (legal advice and attorney-client communications), No. 14 (legal advice and attorney-client communications), and No. 22 (attorney-client advice and litigation communications).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Flags Interrogatory No. 11 as premature contention
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo explicitly identifies Interrogatory No. 11 as a contention interrogatory in the global 'Contention timing' section and again in the specific No. 11 response, recommending deferral or only a limited present-knowledge answer.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Flags Interrogatory No. 18 as premature contention
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies Interrogatory No. 18 as a “Contention interrogatory” and advises seeking deferral under CMO ¶ 9, thereby flagging it as premature contention discovery.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Flags Interrogatory No. 26 as premature contention
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies Interrogatory No. 26 as seeking contention/legal positions in the global 'Contention timing' section and, in the specific No. 26 discussion, states to object to it as 'premature contention discovery.'

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Cites FRCP 33(a)(2) for deferral of contention interrogatories
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo discusses deferring contention interrogatories under CMO ¶ 9, but it does not cite FRCP 33(a)(2), Rule 33(a)(2), or Fed. R. Civ. P. 33(a)(2) in connection with that objection.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Recommends seeking deferral of contention interrogatories
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies Nos. 11, 18, 25, and 26 as contention interrogatories, recommends objecting to them as premature, and advises seeking stipulation or court deferral under CMO ¶ 9. It also notes the fact discovery cutoff of August 15, 2025.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Flags temporal overbreadth (from 2009 to present)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly objects to the 'Relevant Period (2009--present)' globally and repeatedly flags the 2009-to-present/16-year scope as overbroad or disproportionate for multiple interrogatories, including Nos. 2, 5, 9, 15, and 24.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Notes FASA effective date limits relevant period
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo objects to the 2009-present period as overbroad and sometimes proposes narrowing to the FASA term or 2018 onward, but it does not state that the FASA was executed/effective March 1, 2018, nor does it identify the alleged wrongful conduct period as Q3 2021 to Q2 2022 as the basis for narrowing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Recommends narrowed temporal counter-proposal
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo repeatedly objects to overbroad temporal scopes such as 2009-present and proposes specific narrowed periods tied to the FASA term or alleged conduct, including 2018-present, 2020-2022, 2018-2024, Q1 2018-Q4 2024, and other account-specific date ranges.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Flags Interrogatory No. 12 as overbroad re: non-party clients
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly flags Interrogatory No. 12 as problematic because it seeks other client identities and individual NAV errors/restatements, citing nonparty privacy/confidentiality, burden, proportionality, and the need for narrowing, anonymization, protective order, and client notice. It also specifically references avoiding a review of 10 years of 39 client files.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Raises third-party confidentiality concerns
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly raises third-party confidentiality concerns for Interrogatory No. 12, stating that client identities, financial data, NAV errors, and remediation details are protected by FASA § 11.2 and implicate nonparty privacy, and recommends client notice, protective order, anonymization, and narrowed disclosure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Raises relevance and/or proportionality objections for No. 12
criteria_results.reasoning: For Interrogatory No. 12, the memo expressly raises objections based on burden and proportionality, noting that other-client NAV error information implicates nonparty privacy and proportionality and proposing narrowed aggregate alternatives rather than client-specific disclosure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Flags Interrogatory No. 20 as seeking work product
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly flags Interrogatory No. 20 as concerning litigation experts/consultants and methodology, objects under Rule 26(b)(3) and 26(b)(4), and states that non-testifying consultant facts/opinions and counsel-directed methodology/findings are protected work product/trial-preparation material.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Cites FRCP 26(b)(3) and/or 26(b)(4)
criteria_results.reasoning: In the section for Interrogatory No. 20, the memo expressly objects on the ground that the request is “protected under Rules 26(b)(3), 26(b)(4)(B)--(D), and CMO ¶ 13,” which directly cites FRCP 26(b)(3) and 26(b)(4) in connection with that interrogatory.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Notes expert disclosures not yet due
criteria_results.reasoning: Interrogatory No. 20 expressly objects as premature under Rule 26(b)(4) and CMO ¶ 13, and it references the expert schedule, including affirmative expert disclosures on Sept. 15, rebuttal on Oct. 15, and expert depositions by Nov. 14, 2025. Thus it notes the relevant expert discovery deadline and treats the interrogatory as premature/protected.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Flags absurd definition of 'communication'
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly flags the Definitions/Instructions issue by identifying “telepathic impressions” and “subliminal messaging” in the definition of “Communication” and stating they are outside any reasonable, relevant construction, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Flags overbroad 'relating to' definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo objects to several definitions/instructions (e.g., Relevant Period, You, Identify, Communication), but it does not specifically identify or flag an overbroad definition of “relating to” such as “in any way logically connected to” as objectionable.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Flags Interrogatories No. 8, 16, 28 as de facto doc requests
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly flags No. 8 as an “all documents” catalog duplicating Rule 34 and No. 28 as a demand to catalog every document as an interrogatory. It also notes document-request concerns for No. 16. Thus at least two of the three targeted interrogatories are identified as de facto document requests.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Distinguishes FRCP 33 from FRCP 34
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly objects to interrogatories that function as an “all documents” catalog duplicating Rule 34 production and states that a demand to catalog every document is improper as an interrogatory, while suggesting Rule 33(d) only for specified business records. This sufficiently distinguishes Rule 33 interrogatories from Rule 34 document requests and notes that interrogatories should not substitute for document requests.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Mentions FRCP 33(d) business records option
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo explicitly references Rule 33(d) multiple times, including a global instruction to use Rule 33(d) where answers can be derived from specified business records and numerous interrogatory-specific suggestions to use Rule 33(d) with Bates ranges or precise record references.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Flags Interrogatory No. 19 re: Roszak's private info
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo specifically addresses Interrogatory No. 19, flags Roszak’s Social Security number and subsequent-employer/current compensation as highly private, irrelevant, and disproportionate, and notes Whitmore lacks or need not investigate current employer/compensation details. This satisfies the privacy/proportionality concern required by the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Recommends narrowed response for Roszak contact info
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo specifically recommends a narrowed response for Roszak: provide last-known witness contact information, including last-known address and a verified last-confirmed personal cell, while objecting to Social Security number and current/subsequent-employer compensation as private, irrelevant, and disproportionate.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Flags Interrogatory No. 25 as calling for legal conclusions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly flags Interrogatory No. 25 under the heading “Legal position on validity/scope of § 9.1,” objects that it demands legal analysis, and states that any limited response would contend § 9.1 is valid and enforceable and covers the claims. This satisfies the requirement to identify No. 25 as objectionable for seeking a legal conclusion about the validity/enforceability of the arbitration clause.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Applies FRCP 26(b)(1) proportionality analysis
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo repeatedly applies proportionality concepts to specific interrogatories, objecting to broad requests as disproportionate or not proportional and discussing burden, confidentiality, narrowed time periods, and aggregate alternatives (e.g., Interrogatories 2, 12, 15, 17, and 24). Although it does not explicitly cite Rule 26(b)(1), it references and applies the proportionality standard to particular requests.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies specific interrogatories with strongest proportionality objections
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo specifically flags Interrogatory No. 12 as subject to strong objections including burden and proportionality, No. 15 as not proportional and burdensome, and No. 24 as burdensome and disproportionate. Thus it identifies at least two of the specified interrogatories as having strong proportionality objections.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Flags arbitration waiver risk
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly includes an arbitration-rights reservation for all discovery responses, routes Nos. 25–26 to lead counsel, and warns that a reservation is not a safe harbor from waiver and that counsel must assess when to move to compel arbitration. It also notes for No. 26 that a discovery reservation alone does not determine waiver. This sufficiently flags the arbitration waiver risk associated with responding to arbitration-related interrogatories.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Recommends express reservation of arbitration rights
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly recommends including a standing arbitration reservation in the response preamble, specifically reserving Whitmore's rights under FASA Section 9.1 and referencing it for arbitration-related interrogatories Nos. 25–26.

criteria_results.title: Response strategy categories used for each interrogatory
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo provides an interrogatory-by-interrogatory recommended strategy, with each entry indicating whether to answer, object, answer subject to objections, refuse/withhold based on privilege or prematurity, or propose narrowing/protective measures. Although it does not use the exact labels listed in the criterion, the categories substantially correspond to them throughout.

criteria_results.title: Memo addresses all 30 interrogatories
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo explicitly includes an interrogatory-by-interrogatory strategy section with separate entries for Nos. 1 through 30, so none of the 30 interrogatories are omitted.

criteria_results.title: Correct case name
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo identifies the case as “Trident Growth Fund III LP v. Whitmore Capital Advisors LLC,” which matches the required case name exactly.

criteria_results.title: Correct case number
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo identifies the case as "Case No. 24-cv-08341-LTS (S.D.N.Y.)," which matches the required case number.

criteria_results.title: Correct court
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo identifies the case as pending in the Southern District of New York by listing the case number followed by “(S.D.N.Y.).”

criteria_results.title: Correct interrogatory response deadline
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo explicitly states that the interrogatories were served February 3, 2025 and that responses and specific objections are due March 5, 2025 under Rule 33(b)(2).

criteria_results.title: Correctly references FASA Section 9.1 arbitration clause
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo repeatedly references FASA § 9.1 as the arbitration clause, including Whitmore's reservation of rights to compel arbitration, and specifically notes that the clause specifies JAMS and Hartford as the forum/seat. Thus it correctly identifies the section and arbitration mechanism required by the criterion.

criteria_results.title: FASA Section 8.3 liability cap section reference
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo explicitly and correctly identifies FASA § 8.3 as the liability cap / limitation of liability provision, including in the contract guardrails section and Interrogatory No. 11 discussion.

criteria_results.title: FASA Section 8.3 liability cap amount
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo references a potential $496,000 cap but does not state the required formula that FASA § 8.3 caps liability at 2× the prior 12 months’ fees. Instead, it describes the cap as based on fees actually paid in the prior 12 months, which omits the 2× multiplier and is materially incomplete under the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Identifies unobjectionable interrogatories as proper
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo does not only flag problematic interrogatories; it affirmatively states that some should be answered with little or no objection. For example, No. 1 is described as “mostly answerable” with “no need for boilerplate relevance objection,” No. 29 says “No material relevance objection,” and No. 30 says to “Answer fully” consistent with Rule 26. These confirm at least some interrogatories are proper or largely unobjectionable.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies damages amount of $14.7 million
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo does not identify the alleged damages amount as approximately $14.7 million anywhere. Although it does not appear to materially misstate that figure, it omits the required damages amount entirely, so it does not satisfy the criterion.

criteria_results.title: References the three portfolio companies at issue
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo references MedStream in connection with the NAV/valuation issues, but it does not name or otherwise correctly identify Cipherion Technologies LLC or NovaPharma Holdings Inc. Because fewer than two of the three portfolio companies are named correctly, the criterion is not satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: References FASA Section 11.2 confidentiality obligations
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo specifically addresses Interrogatory No. 12 and states that client identities, financial data, NAV errors, and remediation details are protected by FASA § 11.2, using that contractual confidentiality obligation as a basis for objection.
